jobs.title: Environmental Health Safety Specialist
jobs.description:
Title: Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) Specialist

Department: Human Resources
Role Scope: The EHS Specialist will be responsible for implementing and maintaining workplace safety programs, conducting inspections and risk assessments, supporting incident investigations, coordinating required training, and helping ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, and local health and safety requirements, including California OSHA (Cal/OSHA) regulations.

Specific Activities:

Support the development, implementation, and ongoing maintenance of the Company's Environmental, Health & Safety programs.
Maintain and update safety policies, procedures, programs, and related documentation.
Support the company's Injury and Illness Prevention Program (IIPP) and other required written safety programs.
Conduct regular workplace inspections and safety audits across manufacturing, production, warehouse, laboratory, and office areas to
Identify potential hazards and recommend practical corrective and preventive actions; monitor corrective actions to ensure identified hazards are addressed in a timely manner.
Partner with managers and employees to address safety concerns and promote a strong safety culture.
Assist with regulatory inspections, audits, and responses to findings.
Support the investigation and documentation of workplace injuries, illnesses, incidents, near misses, and other safety-related events.
Partner with HR, management, employees, and workers' compensation partners as appropriate regarding workplace injuries and claims.
Maintain accurate EHS records and documentation in accordance with applicable requirements.
Support return-to-work and workplace accommodation processes as appropriate, in partnership with HR and management.
Support applicable environmental compliance activities, including hazardous materials, hazardous waste, chemical storage, and related programs.
Maintain required permits, logs, records, and documentation as assigned.
Support emergency preparedness planning, drills, and response procedures.
Assist with maintaining emergency response supplies and safety equipment.
Evaluate hazards associated with manufacturing, production, warehouse, equipment, machinery, chemicals, ergonomics, and material handling activities.
Assist with machine guarding, lockout/tagout, hazard communication, PPE, emergency preparedness, and other applicable safety programs.
Support ergonomic assessments and recommend appropriate controls or improvements.
Coordinate and/or conduct required EHS training for employees, supervisors, and managers.
Maintain training records and monitor completion of required training.
Develop safety communications, toolbox talks, presentations, and other educational materials.
Promote employee awareness and participation in safety programs.
Provide guidance to managers and employees regarding safe work practices and applicable safety requirements.
Other duties and special projects as assigned.

Key Competencies:

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Health & Safety, Occupational Safety, Industrial Hygiene, Environmental Science, or a related field preferred.
Equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant experience may be considered.
3+ years’ of environmental, health & safety experience, preferably in a biomedical manufacturing organization.  
Bilingual in English/Spanish is required. Must be able to speak, write, and read in English and Spanish.  
Strong presentation, training and facilitation, and project management skills are essential.  
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with employees at all levels of the organization.
Able to work independently as well as within a team.  
Proficiency in LEAN and Continuous Improvement manufacturing principles.  
Knowledge of California specific environmental and workplace safety requirements.
Experience with EHS management systems or electronic safety/compliance platforms.
EHS-related certification such as ASP, CSP, CIH, or equivalent.
Ability to stand for large amounts of time.  
Ability to lift up to 25 lbs.  

Reports To: HR Director
Compensation: Non-Exempt

jobs.title: PART TIME WATERSHED INSPECTOR
jobs.description:
Summary Description

Start or expand your environmental career at the City of San Marcos’ Watershed Program! Are you looking for hands-on experience in environmental regulation? Join our team as a Part-Time Watershed Inspector. This isn’t just a role—it’s a chance to build your resume and gain technical field experience while directly protecting our local water quality.

You’ll spend the majority of your time in the field, where you’ll play a key role in following up on community concerns and helping resolve stormwater pollution concerns. Working under the direction of the Watershed Program Manager and supervision of the Watershed Administrator, you will be a vital part of the team assisting in the implementation of the City’s Stormwater Municipal Code.

WHY JOIN US?

Flexible Scheduling: We understand that life is busy. Whether you are balancing a degree, family, or other projects, we offer a flexible part-time schedule designed to work around your commitments.
Resume-Building Experience: Gain direct, "boots-on-the-ground" experience in municipal government and stormwater regulation.
Work Outdoors: Swap the cubicle for the outdoors! A Watershed Inspector will be primarily responsible for field duties.

What You'll Do

Field Investigations (Primary):
Perform patrols and investigations related to the Illicit Discharge Detection and Elimination (IDDE) program.
Respond to and document watershed concerns reported by the public or internal staff.
Schedule and perform follow-up inspections to ensure continued environmental health.
Verify inventories for Structural Best Management Practices (SBMPs).
Participate in occasional weekend outreach events to connect with the community.

Data, Excel & Office Support (Occasional):
Maintain inventories and databases for permit tracking requirements, utilize Excel to analyze numerical data and organize it for management review.
Prepare enforcement correspondence in accordance with the City's Enforcement Response Plan.
Draft or update written Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for the Watershed Program.
Assist with the development and review of public education, outreach, and training materials.

Community Collaboration:
Build positive working relationships with co-workers and the public using excellent customer service.

Hours Required

While flexible based on the candidate’s personal schedule, the successful candidate will work an average of 20 hours per week. As a part-time employee, the Watershed Inspector may work up to 999 hours per fiscal year. Scheduled hours will depend upon the Department’s need and budget approval.

RECRUITMENT TIMELINE

APPLICATIONS ACCEPTED
Applications accepted beginning August 10, 2026

APPLICATIONS DUE
Applications must be received by 4:00pm, August 31, 2026

FIRST INTERVIEWS
September 21, 2026

REPRESENTATIVE DUTIES

Learn more about the part time Watershed Inspector role.

jobs.title: Environmental Science Specialist
jobs.description:
We’re hiring PhD researchers and early-career scientists in Environmental Science
for a remote AI research and scientific data validation project supporting Google Gemini
.
If you have a strong research background and experience working with scientific literature, datasets, or research databases, this is an opportunity to apply your expertise to next-generation AI systems.

🔬 Who We’re Looking For
Environmental Science researchers
Climate researchers
Ecologists
Environmental modelling specialists
Sustainability / environmental researchers
Recent PhD graduates
Postdoctoral researchers
Early-career researchers

📌 What You’ll Do
Review and evaluate scientific content and research data
Validate information against peer-reviewed literature and trusted datasets
Identify inaccurate, incomplete, or inconsistent scientific information
Curate, classify, and organize scientific data
Perform data annotation and quality assurance
Evaluate the reliability and relevance of research outputs
Apply scientific reasoning to AI-generated research content
Document findings and communicate recommendations

✅ Requirements
PhD completed or recently completed in Environmental Science or a relevant discipline
0–5 years of relevant experience

Strong research experience through publications, thesis work, field/lab research, or postdoctoral projects
Familiarity with scientific datasets, repositories, or research databases
Strong understanding of scientific research methodology and literature
Excellent analytical and critical-thinking skills
Strong written English communication

⭐ Good to Have
Scientific data curation or quality-review experience
Environmental datasets or research databases
Literature review / fact-checking experience
AI evaluation, annotation, or data-labeling experience
Experience with AI-assisted research tools

💼 Engagement
Role:
Environmental Science Researcher / Scientific Data Validator
Project:
AI Research & Scientific Data Validation
Client:
Google Gemini
Work Mode:
Remote
Hours:
25–35 hours/week
Contract:
1099 / Independent Contractor
